title: Signal handling: Ctrl-C aborts every child-process loop
summary: Foreground children share the caller's job group, so a terminal Ctrl-C reaches wt and the child alike; wt never signals the child for it. wt's own receipt of SIGINT/SIGTERM while a child runs is the cancellation evidence: once the child exits, every foreground loop that runs multiple child processes (`wt step for-each`, hook pipelines, alias steps, concurrent groups) MUST start nothing more and exit interrupted, instead of charging into the next iteration: otherwise one Ctrl-C against `wt merge` runs the remaining hook steps, with FailureStrategy::Warn silently swallowing each interrupt. Detect via `err.interrupt_signal()` (the worktrunk::git::ErrorExt trait) and propagate WorktrunkError::Interrupted; the check happens before any FailureStrategy branch. Never infer cancellation from a numeric exit code such as 130. A final interactive child (pager, --execute program, custom subcommand, an alias's last serial step) owns the key as input instead. See AGENTS.md > Signal Handling and src/signal_forwarder.rs.
